paragraphs.text: # chat-message-export
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that exports chat content as Markdown files.
| Where | Action | Output |
| Each finalized assistant reply's action strip | Download this reply | `deepseek-reply-<timestamp>.

md` |
| Session header | Download the whole visible conversation | `deepseek-conversation-<timestamp
Session header | Download the whole visible conversation | `deepseek-conversation-<timestamp>.md` |

The conversation export reads the Chat store's visible node order: user and
steering messages become

`## User` sections, and each Turn contributes only its
final reply — tool calls and reasoning are s

kipped, so the file reads as a
transcript rather than a log.
## Why user bubbles have no button of their own

The Harness exposes per-message actions only through
`conversation.chat.assistant-actions`, which fi

res for finalized assistant
messages. User-row controls (copy, timestamp) are built into the host co

mponent
with no extension slot, so adding one there would mean re-implementing the whole
user row —

attachments, images, references, pending and echo states — and
tracking upstream markup. The session
-header export covers the user side instead.
## Install
From a DeepSeek Harness session, point `plugin_manager` at this directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package is linked into the active profile, so it applies to every session in
that profile and su

rvives restart. Refresh the Web page afterwards; the browser
assembles client modules at page load.

For a local development loop, the Web client watches its own plugin bundles — a
rebuilt `client.js`
can reload without a page refresh.
## Layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Plain JavaScript — no build step, no dependencies. The browser half registers
through `window.__Modu
leLoader__.load` and contributes two slot entries:

- `conversation.chat.assistant-actions`, id `export`, order `20`
- `conversation.session.header.acti
ons`, id `export-conversation`, order `30`

UI text goes through the Client locale service (`ctx.locale.register`); styles
use only `--dsw-alias

-*` theme tokens, so the buttons follow light and dark
themes. Downloads use a transient `<a downloa

d>` with an object URL, so no Host
route or file write is involved, and the styles tag is removed wh

en the plugin
unloads.
## Package name

`@local/chat-message-export` is a private, unpublished scope. Keep the name in
`package.json`, `clie

nt.js`, `cordis.patch.yml`, and the locale `meta` in sync if
you rename it.
